title: Destructive Move from Mutable Reference
pattern: Moving a value out from behind a mutable reference (&mut T) without immediately replacing it with a valid instance.
why_bad: If a panic or exception occurs before a new value is written back, the compiler will attempt to drop uninitialized or duplicate memory, leading to a catastrophic double-free or memory corruption.
detection: Dereferencing a mutable reference to move the inner value (`let x = *s;`) without using std::mem::take or std::mem::replace.
counterexample: Using std::mem::take or std::mem::swap to safely swap the value out while leaving a default value behind.
fix: Use `std::mem::take` to safely swap the value while leaving a valid default behind: `let was = std::mem::take(s);`.
